title: SCHEMA — Reference
idiom: bold black-and-cream linocut, set-square and plumb bob (hero); icon: a drafting triangle with a pen at its foot ruling a line onward, the rules read at the pen
hero_prompt: Bold linocut print in black on cream paper, thick carved shapes with white gouge marks, no fine hatching, flat and graphic, not a photograph, not a 3D render, no depth-of-field: seen from the side, a large plain wooden set-square standing upright on a bare table, and beside it a plumb bob hanging perfectly still on a straight line from above, the two together the measure of square and true; solid black shapes, generous empty cream space, a quiet plain workroom wall behind.
icon_prompt: Bold linocut emblem printed in black on cream paper, flat single-colour black shapes, no shading or gradients, not a photograph, not a 3D render: a plain black drafting set-square, a right-angled triangle with a triangular hole through its middle, standing with its right angle at the lower left, its upright edge on the left and its flat base along the bottom. From the set-square's right-hand tip one bold straight black line runs on to the right along the ground, and at the end of that line a single plain steel pen nib, pointed and unmarked, leans forward, still drawing it. No pen holder, no hand. The set-square is completely bare: no graduations, no ticks, no scale, no markings of any kind on its edges. Nothing centred, no circle. Bold, high-contrast, thick shapes only, reads clearly at 24 pixels.
